extracted.intended_audience: patent and industrial-design applicants, representatives/agents, and ARIPO/designated State industrial property offices
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory rules and procedural requirements for filing, examination, publication, grant/registration, fees, post‑grant actions, and inter‑office communications under the Harare Protocol administered by ARIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional patent application (Rule 18bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may file a divisional application relating to any pending earlier ARIPO patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional shall be filed in the language of the proceedings for the earlier application. If the earlier application was not in an official language of the Office, the divisional may be filed in the language of the earlier application but a translation into the language of the proceedings must be filed within 2 months of filing the divisional. The divisional application shall be filed with the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility model not protectable if subject of prior patent/utility model (Rule 18ter(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: No utility model may be protected if it has already been the subject of a patent for an invention or a registration of a utility model based on a prior application or application benefiting from an earlier priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty and industrial applicability for utility models (Rule 18ter(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty and industrial applicability within the jurisdiction of the Contracting States of the Protocol shall be applied with respect to utility models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited/accelerated examination of utility-model applications (Rule 18ter(3)(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request expedited/accelerated examination so a decision on suitability for registration is made within a period specified in the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expedition is subject to conditions: (i) application is for a single invention and/or applicant agrees examination division will consider only the first identified invention; (ii) applicant undertakes to respond immediately to clarifications; (iii) application is not withdrawn and then reinstated before conclusion of examination; (iv) a search report based on acceptable minimum documentation on claims of same or narrower scope than the ARIPO claims is provided. Timeframe for decision is set in Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed commencement of examination for utility models (Rule 18ter(3)(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request delayed commencement of examination for up to 1 year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must include a written explanation satisfactory to the Director General and the application must not be deemed withdrawn due to non-payment of annual maintenance fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office handling of requests to modify examination timeline (Rule 18ter(3)(c),(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall acknowledge requests to modify examination timeline and provide direction upon receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will either (i) direct applicant to remit requisite fees for modification, (ii) confirm concurrence if application relates to defined green technologies, or (iii) indicate modification is not possible with reasons. A request is not considered made unless prescribed fees are paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination of industrial designs follows national laws (Rule 18quater(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination of industrial designs shall be conducted in accordance with the national laws of each designated State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designated-State communications on industrial designs and response timelines (Rule 18quater(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A communication by a designated State pursuant to Section 4(3) is made on its behalf by its industrial property office; where designated State communicates that a registration shall have no effect, the applicant may respond within 3 months and the designated State shall respond within 3 months of receipt of the applicant’s communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for conversion into national application (Rule 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request that the application be treated as an application under national law of one or more designated States may be filed within 3 months from the date of the Office's refusal of the request for reconsideration, and shall specify the designated States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within 2 weeks of receiving such a request, the Office shall transmit copies of the application and all relevant documents to the industrial property offices of the designated States specified by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of publication of ARIPO patent applications (Rule 19bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication of the ARIPO patent application shall contain the description, the claims, abstract and drawings if any, as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The published application shall indicate the designated Contracting State(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party observations after publication (Rule 19ter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Following publication, any person may submit observations concerning the patentability of the invention; observations may be considered if they concern novelty, inventive step, claim clarity, sufficiency of disclosure, patentability of subject matter and unallowable amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations must be filed in writing in English and include a statement of the grounds. Documentary evidence may be filed in any language but Office may request translation into English within a specified period or evidence will be disregarded. The person filing may not become a party to proceedings. Observations should preferably be filed electronically. The Office acknowledges receipt if not anonymous but does not inform further action beyond subsequent published office actions. The Office will endeavour to issue the next office action to communicate substantiated observations to the applicant. If observations call patentability into question they must be taken into account in any proceedings until terminated. Observations alleging prior art from use are taken into account only if facts are not disputed by the applicant/proprietor or are established beyond reasonable doubt. Observations received after decision to grant/refuse are included in the file without noting content. Observations filed during international phase will be considered on entry into the Regional phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant/registration, recordal and publication of patents and utility models (Rule 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon expiry of the 6‑month period and subject to payment of grant/registration and publication fee, the Office shall grant or register the patent or utility model, publish a reference in the ARIPO Journal, record it in the Register, issue a certificate and copy, and transmit copies to each designated State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of reference shall include: patent/utility model number; owner name/address; inventor name/address; applicant's representative; filing date; accepted priority statement and priority date/countries (if claimed); effective date of grant/registration; title; abstract; if drawings, the most illustrative drawing; symbol of International Patent Classification; Contracting States for which granted/registered. Certificate of Grant/Registration must be signed by Director General and contain number, owner, filing/priority dates, effective date, title and Contracting States for which granted/registered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration/recordal and publication of industrial designs (Rule 20bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon expiry of the 6‑month period and payment of fees, the Office shall register the industrial design, publish a reference in the ARIPO Journal, record it in the Industrial Design Register, issue a certificate and copy, and transmit copies to each designated State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication shall include: design number; owner name/address; originator/creator name/address; applicant's representative; filing date; accepted priority statement and priority date/countries (if claimed); effective date of registration; title; most illustrative reproduction; symbol of International Classification; Contracting States for which registered. Certificate of Registration shall be signed by Director General and contain number, owner, filing/priority dates, effective date, title and Contracting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and timing of annual maintenance fees (Rule 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual maintenance fees payable under Sections of the Protocol shall be as prescribed in the Schedule of Fees. Maintenance fees already due for a 'mother' application at the date a divisional is filed shall also be paid for the divisional and shall be due on its filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance fees fall due on the eve of each anniversary of filing and must be paid in advance. A 6‑month period of grace is allowed subject to payment of prescribed surcharge. Failure to pay results in deemed withdrawal of application or lapse of patent. If rights are re-established under Rule 24 certain maintenance fees that fell due during loss of rights become due on notification of re-establishment; others may be paid within 6 months from the notification provided surcharge is paid. The Office shall record each lapsed patent and publish notification of lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for request for limitation (post‑grant amendment) (Rule 21bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for limitation of an ARIPO patent or utility model shall be filed in writing and contain specified particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must contain: (a) particulars of the proprietor (as in Rule 5(5)(c)) and an indication of the Contracting States for which requester is proprietor; (b) patent number; (c) complete version of amended claims and, if applicable, amended description and drawings; (d) particulars of representative if appointed (as in Rule 5(5)(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: General communications and Administrative Instructions (Rule 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications between the Office and industrial property offices of Contracting States shall be effected directly by registered mail or any other safe electronic means. Communications with courts or other authorities shall be through the intermediary of the industrial property office of the said States and subject to the same rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industrial property offices of designated States that provide for registration of licences, assignments and similar rights shall, upon registering such rights with respect to patents, utility models and industrial designs, promptly provide the Office with particulars. The Office shall record in the Registers all such notifications. The Director General shall establish Administrative Instructions dealing with application details; these Instructions shall specify time limits not fixed by the Protocol, manner of computation of time limits and conditions for extensions, and minima and maxima for time limits to be determined by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of assignments, licences and other similar rights (Rule 22bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment of a patent, industrial design or utility model granted or registered shall be registered in the appropriate Register at the application of any interested party upon production of documents satisfying the Office that the transfer has taken place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application is not fulfilled until prescribed fee is paid; Office may reject application only for failure to comply with required conditions. Assignment has effect vis‑à‑vis the Office only when and to the extent documents have been produced. Paragraphs apply mutatis mutandis to registration of a licence. Registration may be cancelled upon application by any interested party on payment of prescribed fee supported by documents establishing lapse or by a declaration of consent from licensee/proprietor; cancellation application may be rejected if conditions not fulfilled.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (PCT) applications filed with ARIPO as receiving Office (Rule 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an international application is filed with the Office as receiving Office under Section 3bis(3), transmittal fee per PCT Rule 14 is as prescribed; applicant may be represented by attorney/agent with right to represent before an industrial property office of a Contracting State bound by the PCT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications under Section 3bis(4) and (5) the applicant must, within 31 months from filing or priority date: (a) furnish an English translation if published in a language other than English; (b) pay application fee, designation fees per country, and subject to Section 3bis(6)(ii) annual maintenance fees that have become due; (c) appoint a representative if applicant's ordinary residence/principal place of business is not in a Contracting State bound by the PCT; (d) specify the application documents (as filed or as amended) on which ARIPO grant procedure is to be based. Applicant shall file request for examination as provided in Section 3(3) and Rule 18(1). International search and preliminary examination reports for which ARIPO acts as designated/elected Office shall be taken into consideration for Rule 18(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for re‑establishment of rights (Rule 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for re‑establishment of rights under Section 5bis shall be filed in writing within 2 months of removal of cause of non‑compliance but at latest within 1 year of expiry of the unobserved time limit, except certain periods where the request must be filed within 2 months of expiry of that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request is not deemed filed until prescribed fee is paid. The request must state grounds and set out facts relied upon. The omitted act shall be completed within the relevant period for filing the request. The request is deemed filed upon payment of the restoration fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed fees and schedule requirements (Schedules I etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for application, designation, substantive examination requests, searches, publication, page/claim surcharges, grant, annual maintenance (per designated State), surcharges for late payment, corrections, copies, transmittals, conversions, expedited/delayed examination, and many other services are prescribed in the Schedule of Fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of prescribed fees is a recurring requirement across many procedural actions, and many Rules state that requests or filings are not considered made or are not fulfilled until prescribed fees are paid. Fee amounts and conditions (e.g., electronic filing discount) are itemised in the Schedule (PATENTS, UTILITY MODELS, INDUSTRIAL DESIGNS). Examples: application fee, designation fee per State, request for substantive examination fee, prior art search fee, publication fee, claim fees after certain number of claims, grant fee, annual maintenance fees per anniversary, surcharges for late payment, fees for corrections, certified copies, restoration, expedited examination fees, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of prescribed forms and documentary requirements (Schedule II / forms list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific numbered ARIPO forms are designated for particular procedural requests and communications (e.g., Request for alteration of name/address; Request for copies of extracts; Request for grant; Appointment of representative; Request for substantive examination; Notification of decision refusing application; Request to reconsider refusal; Notification of decision to grant; Certificate forms; Request for expedited/delayed examination; Request for conversion into national application; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and representatives must use appropriate forms for the corresponding actions as listed in Schedule II; many Rules reference particular forms (e.g., Form No. 13 Request for substantive examination). Forms include required fields and are part of the documentary compliance requirements.
